genericProblem: A governed browser L2 can report green without proving the complete approved application topology, request-to-owner data path, readback, and cleanup boundary when its runner, fixture, or UI specs use stale routes, incomplete inputs, or unobservable integration edges.
rootCause: The executable joint browser-L2 denominator was not reconstructed from the governed environment matrix: a platform-only persistent local runner and design-era P6-3 registry were mistaken for a complete joint proof, while the current execution topology was corrected to local applications and browser with remote middleware only. The joint fixture also retained platform invitation HTTP calls after the accepted retirement removed that adapter face, confusing the retired HTTP adapter with the still-owned invitation capability. The L2 then exposed two distinct JSON runtime compatibility boundaries: generated edge DTOs used Jackson 2 `JsonNode` against the Spring Boot 4 Jackson 3 HTTP converter, and the contract owner receipt's correctly module-discovering Jackson 2 mapper had no declared Java-time module for its `StoreContractReadback` LocalDate fields. Once the fixture passed, a third infrastructure defect became observable: the managed runner stored only a subprocess-output hash/length and a truncated failure string, leaving no readable redacted command artifact for the first Playwright failure. That diagnostic revealed the remaining integration defect: the fixture never reconciled its private test-input set with the platform spec environment denominator, and it wrote account-identifying operation inputs into its public result instead of the 0600 private environment. The repaired fixture then revealed the platform-IAM owner list had treated optional absent text filters as untyped PostgreSQL parameters and a null-hostile `List.of` copy, so the IA03 default administrator list failed before it could read an owner page. After shared JSON media-type repair passed platform login, the same nullable PostgreSQL boundary emerged in the IA02 workspace-management owner list: absent optional filters were untyped in the count and page predicates, preventing the enabled workspace selector and list from loading. The next platform run exposed three independent browser-proof defects: runner-level parallel workers reused a fixture-created identity/source whose correct owner rate-limit lock serializes BCrypt login and session creation; a shared selector helper addressed a hidden Ant Design virtual-list option; and an IA02 Drawer proof expected an absent automation anchor. The corrected runner serializes each app batch without weakening production locks or minting accounts, and the helper/Drawer bind only rendered approved controls. That longer fixture run also exposed the observability gap that its internal progress was buffered until completion, preventing a 30-second diagnosis; an exact-set failure hid even its safe missing/extra key-name diff. A subsequent operations run exposed a shared owner transaction boundary defect: StoreCandidateTaskReadService probed five target families by calling the throwing single-target task-path API inside one REQUIRED transaction and catching each normal not-found. The caught owner exception still marked the transaction rollback-only, so a successful candidate response became UnexpectedRollbackException at commit. The reusable repair is to use the non-throwing owner availability read to select exactly one target family, then perform one bounded path read; never catch expected not-found exceptions from a REQUIRED owner call inside the same transaction.
finiteDenominator: one local platform runner
two registry drift paths
nine absent specs
one incomplete recovery spec
nine existing platform specs
seven U11 joint-fixture retired platform invitation HTTP consumers
four dangling root OpenAPI invitation pointers
one out-of-package platform-only fixture consumer recorded but not modified
sixteen generated edge DTOs with object-valued fields and four mapper consumers
seven owner command receipt serializers: one contract receipt serializes a LocalDate-bearing readback; six others have no Java-time-bearing current readback boundary
five managed runner subprocess boundaries (local start, owner fixture, platform Playwright, operations Playwright, local stop)
forty-four declared browser environment inputs: fourteen platform and thirty operations/public keys, each sourced from an approved owner readback or private credential input
two fixture result channels: public redacted fixture JSON and the 0600 private environment file
one platform-IAM owner list predicate with its directly derived pagination bind collection and three nullable filter pairs (userName, loginName, status)
one workspace-management owner list with count/page parity and four nullable filter pairs (name, groupWorkspaceKey, operationsTitle, status)
all fixture owner HTTP/bootstrap stages and the one exact browser-input set assertion
two app-specific exact Playwright batches that reuse fixture-created login identities and their owner identity/source rate-limit locks
two shared platform Ant Design selection helpers and one IA02 workspace detail Drawer automation anchor
one StoreCandidateTaskReadService visible-scope resolver and its five target-family probes
counterexamples: remote Testcontainers is not browser L2
remote middleware does not require remote application or browser execution
operations/public invitation contracts remain retained although platform invitation HTTP is retired
Jackson 2 owner-internal persistence remains valid where the owning module declares all modules required by its own result type; this does not make Jackson 2 types valid edge HTTP transport types
a subprocess whose output cannot contain user secrets still uses the same diagnostic artifact shape; command exit code alone is never the evidence

a public owner-returned business label or route locator may be recorded in the redacted fixture JSON; a login name, mobile number, password, cookie, OTP, token, grant or account-identifying test value may not
mandatory pagination and sort parameters are never absent and therefore do not enter the nullable-parameter denominator
a short pure fixture operation still records its phase but does not require an artificial polling heartbeat
tests with independently provisioned identities and non-overlapping owner rate-limit buckets may use their approved worker policy after proving that separation
owner APIs that return a non-throwing availability set or batch read are not subject to the caught-exception rollback trap; expected absence handling remains inside the owner method
minimalReusableFix: purpose-bound local joint runner/fixture using a managed tunnel and isolated remote middleware namespace, plus exact existing-route specs. A retired invitation HTTP fixture dependency is replaced only by a short-lived WebApplicationType.NONE owner bootstrap that reads enabled workspace state and invokes WorkspaceInvitationService.create with one explicit target intent, writing the raw token only to a run-scoped 0600 private file. Generated edge DTOs use the active HTTP converter's Jackson 3 type universe; owner-local receipt serializers keep their own Jackson 2 boundary and directly declare each module required by their current API readback types, including Java-time for contract LocalDate fields. Every managed subprocess writes its sanitized stdout/stderr to a run-scoped 0600 diagnostic file before its phase event records the path, hash and byte count; sanitization replaces every security-sensitive or account-identifying value supplied through its environment before persistence, and the existing runner self-test proves a supplied secret cannot survive the artifact. The fixture derives every platform and operations/browser input from the same owner readback or approved private credential input that established the preceding fact, checks the exact union of spec-required environment keys, and writes account-identifying values only to the 0600 private environment while public fixture JSON retains only redacted labels and route locators. Owner queries with optional filters bind absent values as explicit text and copy those same values through a null-tolerant collection without changing owner filtering, total, ordering or pagination. Shared-identity browser batches run one worker per app; shared Ant Design locators select only rendered visible options and approved drawers expose a stable automation anchor. Fixture stages synchronously append redacted 0600 JSONL phase records and exact-set failures enumerate only missing/extra key names. For owner scope resolution, use the owner-provided non-throwing availability/batch APIs to resolve one valid target family before a bounded path read; do not loop over a throwing REQUIRED owner call and catch its expected not-found exception in the caller transaction.

prevention.evidence: local process and tunnel identity, remote namespace readback, exact test set, and split cleanup
retired platform invitation route scan, root OpenAPI reference closure, owner-bootstrap focused test and private token output boundary
finite receipt-serializer/type-module scan, module dependency declaration, focused owner receipt replay and fresh managed L2
redacted command artifact with secret-red mutation, phase diagnostic path/hash and fresh L2 first-failure readback
spec-required environment exact-set, owner-readback fixture source review, 0600 private-result boundary and fresh joint L2
IA03 default-list source, typed-null owner query focused proof and fresh joint L2 administrator page
IA02 default workspace-list source, typed-null count/page predicate focused proof and fresh joint L2 workspace selector/list
shared-identity login-lock denominator, one-worker runner invocation, rendered-control locator review and fresh joint L2 business/cleanup result
owner scope resolver transaction boundary, non-throwing availability/batch contract, focused owner proof and fresh candidate endpoint L2 readback

findings.evidence: The executable joint browser-L2 denominator was not reconstructed from the governed environment matrix: a platform-only persistent local runner and design-era P6-3 registry were mistaken for a complete joint proof, while the current execution topology was corrected to local applications and browser with remote middleware only. The joint fixture also retained platform invitation HTTP calls after the accepted retirement removed that adapter face, confusing the retired HTTP adapter with the still-owned invitation capability. The L2 then exposed two distinct JSON runtime compatibility boundaries: generated edge DTOs used Jackson 2 `JsonNode` against the Spring Boot 4 Jackson 3 HTTP converter, and the contract owner receipt's correctly module-discovering Jackson 2 mapper had no declared Java-time module for its `StoreContractReadback` LocalDate fields. Once the fixture passed, a third infrastructure defect became observable: the managed runner stored only a subprocess-output hash/length and a truncated failure string, leaving no readable redacted command artifact for the first Playwright failure. That diagnostic revealed the remaining integration defect: the fixture never reconciled its private test-input set with the platform spec environment denominator, and it wrote account-identifying operation inputs into its public result instead of the 0600 private environment. The repaired fixture then revealed the platform-IAM owner list had treated optional absent text filters as untyped PostgreSQL parameters and a null-hostile `List.of` copy, so the IA03 default administrator list failed before it could read an owner page. After shared JSON media-type repair passed platform login, the same nullable PostgreSQL boundary emerged in the IA02 workspace-management owner list: absent optional filters were untyped in the count and page predicates, preventing the enabled workspace selector and list from loading. The corrected runner serializes each app batch without weakening production locks or minting accounts, and the helper/Drawer bind only rendered approved controls. That longer fixture run also exposed the observability gap that its internal progress was buffered until completion, preventing a 30-second diagnosis; an exact-set failure hid even its safe missing/extra key-name diff. A subsequent operations run exposed a shared owner transaction boundary defect: StoreCandidateTaskReadService probed five target families by calling the throwing single-target task-path API inside one REQUIRED transaction and catching each normal not-found. The caught owner exception still marked the transaction rollback-only, so a successful candidate response became UnexpectedRollbackException at commit. findings.evidence: The fresh platform-admin browser proof showed the approved detail-first edit actions for workspace, role, administrator and account management closing their owner detail Drawers without rendering the queued independent edit/status/action surface within the bounded observation window. The source scan found the same pending-action/afterOpenChange handoff in all four pages. A ref-synchronized pending value alone did not change the failure. The finite root cause was the shared read-only detail Drawer contract using destroyOnHidden: the detail surface was destroyed during its close motion before the post-close handoff could reliably deliver the queued action. Removing destroyOnHidden from the four read-only detail Drawers preserved the mounted lifecycle and the same fresh browser run then passed all four handoffs and their write/readback assertions. The same run also showed that an Ant Design Modal root test-id may remain hidden for motion while its approved dialog is visible, so visibility must bind to the rendered dialog surface rather than its motion wrapper.
findings.minimumFix: Keep every read-only detail Drawer mounted through its close animation, consume each pending action once from the existing post-close callback (a ref may guard the pending value), and preserve the IA requirement that the detail surface closes before the independent action surface opens. Bind save-result L2 visibility to the visible approved Modal dialog and use the existing confirmation control test-id for the next action. Add focused source proof that detail surfaces are not destroyOnHidden plus fresh browser request/readback evidence for every changed write surface; do not open overlays concurrently, add arbitrary delays, or assert Redux internals.
